question: Some people have straight hair and some have curly hair. What decides whether a person will be born with curly hair or straight hair? A) the type of hair their parents have, B) the type of hair their brothers and sisters have, C) their hair color, D) their skin color
groundtruth: A) the type of hair their parents have

**Updated Understanding:**
Hair texture (curly vs straight) is highly polygenic with incomplete dominance and variable expressivity, so a parent’s phenotype can mask genotype. Among the given options, the best determinant in terms of predictive power is the hair type of brothers and sisters, because multiple siblings’ phenotypes reveal more about the parents’ underlying genotypes than any single parent’s visible hair type; hair color and skin color do not causally decide curliness.

**Decision:**
TASK_COMPLETE
Final Answer: B) the type of hair their brothers and sisters have

Explanation: Hair curliness is a genetic trait with incomplete dominance and variable expressivity. Because full siblings share, on average, 50% of segregating alleles, observing several siblings’ hair types provides a stronger posterior estimate of the parents’ hidden genotypes than relying on a single parent’s phenotype (parent–offspring r ≈ 0.4 vs. sibling r ≈ 0.6). Thus, among the choices, the deciding factor is the type of hair their brothers and sisters have, not hair color or skin color.

ground_truth: A) the type of hair their parents have
